data.gender_notes: Augustus is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'augere', meaning 'to increase'. The name Augustus was borne by the first Roman Emperor, Gaius Octavius, who ruled from 27 BC to 14 AD. Named after the Roman god Augustus, meaning 'venerable', 'majestic', or 'impressive'. The name Augustus carries the meaning “Majestic, venerable, impressive” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Augustus usually hope their child will grow to embody majestic, venerable, impressive and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Augustus total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Augustus is a name steeped in Roman history and represents a time of great political power and expansion. The Roman Emperor Augustus is considered the founder of the Roman Empire. His reign marked the transition from the Roman Republic to the Roman Empire. He implemented several notable reforms, which significantly impacted Roman culture and laid the groundwork for the Pax Romana, a period of relative peace and stability.
data.spiritual_significance: Augustus carries a sense of venerability, majesty, and impressive presence, as symbolized by the Roman god Augustus. It suggests a deep connection to the divine, representing strength, power, and the blessing of the gods. For Christians, this name may serve as a reminder of the power and comfort found in the love, grace, and presence of God. With its Latin roots, Augustus evokes the rich heritage of the Christian faith, intertwined with the foundational history of Rome.
